title: Guess the Bible Verse
subtitle: Can you name where these famous verses are found?

questions.text: "For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth on him should not perish, but have eternal life." (John 3:16, ASV) Where is this found?

options.explanation: Yes, this is John 3:16, part of Jesus' night conversation with Nicodemus. It may be the most quoted verse in the whole Bible.
Romans 5:8 is also about God's love, but it speaks of Christ dying for us while we were yet sinners. The wording here is John 3:16.
1 John 4:9 talks about God sending His Son too, but these exact words come from John 3:16.
John 1:14 says the Word became flesh. Close in theme, but not this verse.

questions.text: "In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth." (Genesis 1:1, ASV) Where is this found?

options.explanation: John 1:1 also begins "In the beginning," but it speaks of the Word. This line about creating the heavens and earth opens Genesis.
Correct. This is the very first verse of the Bible, the opening of Genesis.
Psalm 19:1 says the heavens declare the glory of God. A beautiful verse, but not this one.
Hebrews 11:3 says the worlds were framed by the word of God. The exact opening line, though, is Genesis 1:1.

questions.text: "Jehovah is my shepherd; I shall not want." (Psalm 23:1, ASV) Where is this found?

options.explanation: Psalm 100:3 says we are the sheep of His pasture. Related image, but the shepherd line here opens Psalm 23.
John 10:11 is where Jesus calls Himself the good shepherd. This particular verse is from the Psalms.
Yes, this opens the beloved Psalm 23. The ASV uses the name Jehovah where many other versions read LORD.
Isaiah 40:11 pictures God feeding His flock like a shepherd. The wording here belongs to Psalm 23.

questions.text: "Jesus wept." (John 11:35, ASV) Where is this found?

options.explanation: Luke 19:41 says Jesus wept over Jerusalem, but it does not use these two short words. The famous shortest verse is John 11:35.
Correct. This is often called the shortest verse in the Bible. Jesus wept at the tomb of His friend Lazarus.
Matthew 26:75 is where Peter wept bitterly after denying Jesus. The two-word verse is John 11:35.
Mark 14:72 also records Peter weeping. This short verse, though, is from John.

questions.text: "I can do all things in him that strengtheneth me." (Philippians 4:13, ASV) Where is this found?

options.explanation: 2 Corinthians 12:9 is about strength being made perfect in weakness. A close cousin, but not this verse.
Ephesians 6:10 says to be strong in the Lord. The line here, about doing all things through Christ's strength, is Philippians 4:13.
Isaiah 40:31 says those who wait on the Lord renew their strength. Different verse, same encouraging theme.
Yes. Paul wrote this from prison, in the context of being content in any situation.

questions.text: "Trust in Jehovah with all thy heart, And lean not upon thine own understanding." (Proverbs 3:5, ASV) Where is this found?

options.explanation: Correct. Proverbs 3:5 leads into verse 6, which promises that God will direct your paths.
Psalm 37:5 says to commit your way to the Lord. Similar call to trust, but the wording here is Proverbs 3:5.
Jeremiah 17:7 blesses the one who trusts in the Lord. A related promise, but not this exact verse.
Proverbs 16:3 says to commit your works to the Lord. Close in spirit, yet this verse is Proverbs 3:5.

questions.text: "For the wages of sin is death; but the free gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord." (Romans 6:23, ASV) Where is this found?

options.explanation: Romans 3:23 says all have sinned and fall short of God's glory. A neighbor in the same letter, but not this verse.
Romans 5:12 speaks of sin and death entering the world. Related theme, but the line about wages and the free gift is Romans 6:23.
Yes. Romans 6:23 sets the wages of sin against the free gift of eternal life in Christ.
Ephesians 2:8 says we are saved by grace through faith. A wonderful verse on grace, but not this one.

questions.text: "Jesus saith unto him, I am the way, and the truth, and the life: no one cometh unto the Father, but by me." (John 14:6, ASV) Where is this found?

options.explanation: John 10:9 is where Jesus says, "I am the door." Another of His great statements, but not this one.
John 8:12 is "I am the light of the world." Same Gospel, different saying. This verse is John 14:6.
Correct. Jesus said this to Thomas in the upper room, on the night before the cross.
Acts 4:12 says there is no other name by which we must be saved. A matching truth, but spoken by Peter, not here.

questions.text: "Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, And light unto my path." (Psalm 119:105, ASV) Where is this found?

options.explanation: Proverbs 6:23 says the commandment is a lamp. A similar picture, but this exact verse is in Psalm 119.
Yes. This well-loved verse sits in the longest chapter of the Bible, a psalm all about God's word.
Psalm 19:8 says the commandment of the Lord enlightens the eyes. Close in idea, but not this verse.
Matthew 5:14 calls us the light of the world. Different verse, and spoken by Jesus rather than the psalmist.

questions.text: "for all have sinned, and fall short of the glory of God." (Romans 3:23, ASV) Where is this found?

options.explanation: Romans 5:8 shows God's love for sinners, but the line about all falling short is Romans 3:23.
1 John 1:8 warns against claiming we have no sin. A related truth, but not this verse.
Isaiah 53:6 says all we like sheep have gone astray. The same idea in older words, but this exact verse is Romans 3:23.
Correct. Romans 3:23 is a key verse in Paul's case that everyone needs God's grace.

questions.text: "Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called sons of God." (Matthew 5:9, ASV) Where is this found?

options.explanation: Yes. This is one of the Beatitudes from the Sermon on the Mount. The ASV reads "sons of God" here.
Romans 12:18 urges us to live peaceably with everyone. A related call, but the blessing on peacemakers is Matthew 5:9.
James 3:18 speaks of a harvest of righteousness sown in peace. Close in theme, yet not this verse.
Luke 6:20 begins Luke's set of blessings, but this particular Beatitude about peacemakers is found in Matthew 5:9.

scoring.perfectMessage: Incredible. You know exactly where these verses live!
